\section[reciclar]{reciclar — to recycle}

\label{lesson:ES-C504-reciclar}



\begin{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: reciclar}
\textbf{reciclar} — \textquotedblleft{}to recycle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We recycle paper and glass.}
\end{quote}

\section[proteger]{proteger — to protect}

\label{lesson:ES-C504-proteger}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to recycle, then the Spanish for pollution.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: proteger}
\textbf{proteger} — \textquotedblleft{}to protect\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Hay que proteger los bosques.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We must protect the forests.}
\end{quote}

The g becomes j before \emph{o} and \emph{a}: \emph{protejo}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la fábrica]{la fábrica — the factory}

Before the new one: say the Spanish for pollution, then the Spanish for to protect.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la fábrica}

\section[dañar]{dañar — to damage, to harm}

\label{lesson:ES-C504-danar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to protect, then the Spanish for the factory.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: dañar}
\textbf{dañar} — \textquotedblleft{}to damage, to harm\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El sol puede dañar la piel.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The sun can damage your skin.}
\end{quote}

\emph{El daño} is the damage.
